**Finding: deviation (medium) — Section 13, ¶p0047**

The agreement does contain a non-solicitation clause that binds us, not just RadialSpark. It is close to our fallback position:

- **Mutual** — ✓
- **Scope** limited to personnel "who have had direct involvement with the Services" — ✓
- **Duration** one year post-termination — ✓ (well inside the 24-month walk-away line)
- **Solicitation-based, not a no-hire** — ✓ ("solicit for hire," with no standalone prohibition on hiring)
- **General-advertising / unsolicited-approach carve-out** — ✗ missing

Because the carve-out is an express element of the fallback (and the rule summary conditions acceptance on it), the clause as drafted fails the fallback: routine job postings or an inbound approach from a RadialSpark consultant could technically breach it. Everything else stays as negotiated.

**Redline (validated, fallback level, per precedent seed-nosolicit):** appended to Section 13 after "…which shall not be unreasonably withheld.":

> This restriction shall not apply to general advertisements or other recruiting efforts not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or to the hiring of any person who approaches a party on an unsolicited basis.

**Comment:** [Playbook] The mutual non-solicit is otherwise acceptable in duration and scope, so we have only added the customary carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches, consistent with our playbook position that non-solicits must not capture hires we did not target.

Note: the planner flagged this rule as likely absent — the clause is in fact present but located in the Section 7 run-on block (numbered item 13), not near termination.
